source_evidence.anchor: Introduction, global convention for exponents containing +eta
source_evidence.observation: Every exponent containing '+eta' is to be read as holding for any eta > 0.

Logarithmic stability is defined through a relative forward-error bound involving machine epsilon, the condition number raised to chi(n), an O(epsilon^2) term, and chi(n) polynomially bounded in log n.

source_evidence.anchor: Section 3.2 paragraph beginning 'For the rest of this section'
source_evidence.observation: The standing matrix norm for the remainder of Section 3 is the 2-norm.
The theorem first relates fast matrix multiplication to stable inversion, then begins the converse: stable inversion in bit operations, or respectively exact inversion in arithmetic operations.

source_evidence.anchor: Theorem 3.3, continuation at the top of the page
source_evidence.observation: The exact converse concludes that exact matrix inversion in O(n^(omega+eta)) arithmetic operations yields exact matrix multiplication in O(n^(omega+eta)) arithmetic operations.

source_evidence.anchor: unnumbered three-by-three block inverse in the converse proof of Theorem 3.3
source_evidence.observation: The displayed identity is [[I,A,0],[0,I,B],[0,0,I]]^(-1) = [[I,-A,A*B],[0,I,-B],[0,0,I]], with blank lower-triangular blocks understood as zero blocks.

source_evidence.anchor: sentence beginning 'Clearly, inverting the matrix on the left exactly'
source_evidence.observation: The paper explicitly says that exact inversion of the left-hand block matrix permits extraction of the product A*B.

source_evidence.anchor: sentence beginning 'Given only a logarithmically stable inversion routine'
source_evidence.observation: The separate stable converse scales A and B to have norms near one so that the block matrices are well conditioned and inversion needs no extra precision.

source_evidence.anchor: paragraph beginning 'It is tempting to summarize this theorem'
source_evidence.observation: The paper warns that arithmetic-operation and bit-operation complexity must not be conflated; a bit-operation bound does not necessarily organize into an arithmetic-operation bound.

binders: Each occurrence of eta is universally interpreted as an arbitrary eta > 0 (PDF p. 2, printed p. 60, anchor: Introduction global '+eta' convention).

The multiplication inputs are matrices A and B of order n, inherited from Theorem 3.3's n-by-n multiplication problem (PDF p. 11, printed p. 69, anchor: Theorem 3.3 opening; PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: block inverse display).
I is the identity block conforming to A and B; consequently the displayed matrix has three block rows and columns (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: unnumbered three-by-three block inverse).
hypotheses: An exact square-matrix inversion algorithm is available with complexity O(m^(omega+eta)) arithmetic operations for matrix order m (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 69-70, anchor: exact branch of Theorem 3.3).

A and B have the common square dimensions required by the n-by-n multiplication problem; the exact branch states no conditioning, norm, or nonsingularity hypothesis on A or B (PDF p. 11, printed p. 69, anchor: Theorem 3.3; PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: block inverse display).
conclusions: For M = [[I,A,0],[0,I,B],[0,0,I]], the exact inverse is M^(-1) = [[I,-A,A*B],[0,I,-B],[0,0,I]] (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: unnumbered three-by-three block inverse).
The desired ordered product A*B is exactly the block in block row 1, block column 3 of M^(-1) (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: inverse display and following product-extraction sentence).

Therefore exact inversion in O(n^(omega+eta)) arithmetic operations implies exact multiplication in O(n^(omega+eta)) arithmetic operations (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 69-70, anchor: exact converse of Theorem 3.3 and product-extraction sentence).
definitions_and_conventions: Blank entries in the displayed block matrices denote zero blocks, making both matrices unit upper triangular (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: unnumbered block inverse display).

The word 'respectively' pairs stable inversion and stable multiplication under bit-operation accounting, and exact inversion and exact multiplication under arithmetic-operation accounting (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 69-70, anchor: Theorem 3.3 converse).
The notation '+eta' means 'for any eta > 0' throughout the paper (PDF p. 2, printed p. 60, anchor: Introduction global convention).
implicit_context: The enclosing theorem also contains the forward implication from fast arithmetic matrix multiplication to stable inversion in bit operations and a distinct stable converse; the selected block identity supplies the converse reductions (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 69-70, anchor: Theorem 3.3 and its proof).

With n-by-n blocks, M has order 3n; applying an inversion bound to order 3n preserves the stated asymptotic class because 3 is constant. This dimension conversion is implicit rather than spelled out in the extraction sentence (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: three-by-three block display and extraction sentence).

The stable scaling argument following the exact extraction is a sibling branch, not an additional hypothesis for the exact identity or exact reduction (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: consecutive exact-extraction and logarithmically-stable-inversion sentences).
statement.algorithm_linkage: Given A and B, form M = [[I,A,0],[0,I,B],[0,0,I]], invoke the assumed exact inversion routine on M, and read block (1,3) of the returned inverse as A*B. The paper presents this as the converse reduction from exact inversion to exact multiplication (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: unnumbered block inverse and following product-extraction sentence).
numerical_model: The selected branch uses exact arithmetic and counts arithmetic operations, not rounded floating-point operations or bit operations (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 69-70, anchor: exact branch of Theorem 3.3).

Machine epsilon and extra precision belong to the separate logarithmically stable branch and do not enter the exact block identity (PDF p. 7, printed p. 65, anchor: Definition 3.1; PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: exact extraction followed by stable scaling).

The paper explicitly cautions against replacing the arithmetic-operation conclusion by an inference in the opposite direction from a bit-operation bound (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: post-theorem complexity caution).
error_notions: The selected conclusion is exact: the extracted block equals A*B, with no forward-error, backward-error, or relative-error allowance (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: inverse identity and exact product-extraction sentence).

The enclosing stable sibling is governed by logarithmic stability, whose preceding definition uses a relative forward-error bound; that notion must not weaken or replace the exact conclusion (PDF p. 7, printed p. 65, anchor: Definition 3.1; PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: stable converse sentence).
norms: No norm occurs in the exact identity or exact extraction argument (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: block inverse and exact extraction sentence).

The immediately following stable sibling refers to scaling the norms of A and B near one; under the standing Section 3 convention this is the matrix 2-norm (PDF p. 10, printed p. 68, anchor: Section 3.2 norm convention; PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: stable scaling sentence).
constants_and_indexing: The construction has exactly three block rows and three block columns, with A in position (1,2), B in position (2,3), and an explicit zero in position (1,3) before inversion (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: left-hand block matrix).
After inversion, the signs and positions are -A at (1,2), A*B at (1,3), and -B at (2,3), with identity diagonal blocks (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: right-hand block matrix).

For n-by-n A and B, the inversion input is 3n-by-3n; the constant factor three is implicitly absorbed by O(n^(omega+eta)) (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: three-by-three block display and extraction complexity sentence).
The extracted product is A*B in that order, not B*A, and there are no index offsets or summation-index conventions in the result (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: right-hand block matrix).
higher_order_terms: The exact algebraic identity contains no omitted or higher-order numerical terms (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: unnumbered block inverse).

The only big-O term in the selected reduction is the asymptotic operation count O(n^(omega+eta)); no O(epsilon), O(epsilon^2), or approximation term qualifies the extracted product (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: exact extraction sentence and theorem continuation).
exceptional_values: No singularity assumption is imposed on A or B; the constructed matrix is unit upper triangular and its inverse is displayed for the given blocks (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: unnumbered block inverse).

The exact branch states no overflow, underflow, NaN, infinity, division-by-zero, or finite-precision exception assumptions (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 69-70, anchor: exact branch of Theorem 3.3 and its proof).

undebatable_constraints: The left matrix must be [[I,A,0],[0,I,B],[0,0,I]] and the inverse must retain every displayed sign and block position (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: unnumbered three-by-three block inverse).

The recoverable block is exactly A*B at position (1,3); replacing it by B*A, -A*B, or an approximation changes the source claim (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: right-hand inverse and extraction sentence).
The reduction assumes exact inversion and concludes exact multiplication under arithmetic-operation accounting (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 69-70, anchor: exact converse of Theorem 3.3).
The asymptotic exponent is omega+eta, with eta interpreted as arbitrary and positive (PDF p. 2, printed p. 60, anchor: '+eta' convention; PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: theorem continuation).
The constant-size embedding uses a three-by-three block matrix, so an n-by-n multiplication instance becomes a 3n-by-3n inversion instance (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: block inverse display).

No norm, condition-number bound, rounding model, or error tolerance may be added as a requirement of the exact reduction (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: exact extraction sentence preceding the separate stable scaling sentence).
The stable bit-complexity branch and exact arithmetic-complexity branch must remain distinct (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: theorem continuation and post-theorem complexity caution).

ambiguities.issue: The scalar domain is not specified in the theorem or block display (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 69-70, anchor: Theorem 3.3 and block inverse).
ambiguities.evidence: The paper writes only 'matrices' and uses I, A, B, negation, multiplication, and inversion without naming real, complex, field, or ring scalars (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: unnumbered block inverse).
ambiguities.impact: Any formal scalar-domain choice is an interpretation rather than an explicit restriction from this passage (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: unnumbered block inverse).

ambiguities.issue: The block sizes and blank zero blocks are not labeled explicitly inside the display (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: unnumbered block inverse).
ambiguities.evidence: Their n-by-n size is inherited from Theorem 3.3's multiplication problem and from the conformability of the three-by-three block product (PDF p. 11, printed p. 69, anchor: Theorem 3.3; PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: block display).
ambiguities.impact: The source securely supports the common n-by-n specialization; a broader rectangular or unequal-block formulation would be a generalization beyond the stated theorem context (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 69-70, anchors: Theorem 3.3 and block display).

ambiguities.issue: The exact arithmetic-operation model is not further enumerated in the selected passage (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 69-70, anchor: exact branch of Theorem 3.3).
ambiguities.evidence: The theorem counts 'arithmetic operations' but does not specify a primitive-operation set, scalar bit widths, or division costs for the exact branch (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: theorem continuation and complexity caution).
ambiguities.impact: The contract fixes the asymptotic arithmetic-operation claim but cannot derive a more detailed cost model from this passage (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: exact extraction and complexity caution).

ambiguities.issue: The proof does not itemize construction and extraction overhead or explicitly rename the inversion dimension from n to 3n (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: block display and extraction sentence).
ambiguities.evidence: It directly states O(n^(omega+eta)) for inversion of the displayed block matrix and extraction of A*B (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: product-extraction sentence).
ambiguities.impact: Only preservation of the asymptotic class under the constant factor three is justified; no exact operation count or leading constant is supplied (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: block display and extraction sentence).

ambiguities.issue: The stable sibling's phrases 'near 1,' 'very well conditioned,' and 'accurately' are qualitative in this proof paragraph (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: logarithmically stable inversion sentence).
ambiguities.evidence: No numerical threshold or explicit error inequality accompanies those phrases there, although logarithmic stability and the 2-norm are defined earlier (PDF p. 7, printed p. 65, anchor: Definition 3.1; PDF p. 10, printed p. 68, anchor: norm convention; PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: scaling sentence).
ambiguities.impact: Those qualitative stable-branch statements cannot supply extra quantitative hypotheses or conclusions for the selected exact reduction (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: exact extraction followed by stable scaling).

contract_plain_english: For arbitrary eta > 0, assume exact inversion of square matrices costs O(n^(omega+eta)) arithmetic operations (PDF pp. 2 and 11-12, printed pp. 60 and 69-70, anchors: '+eta' convention and exact branch of Theorem 3.3). To multiply n-by-n matrices A and B, invert M = [[I,A,0],[0,I,B],[0,0,I]]. Its exact inverse is [[I,-A,A*B],[0,I,-B],[0,0,I]], so the top-right block is exactly A*B (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchor: unnumbered block inverse and product-extraction sentence). The 3n-by-3n embedding preserves the asymptotic complexity, and the exact claim has no rounding, norm, conditioning, error, or exceptional-value qualification; those belong, where applicable, to the separate stable bit-complexity branch (PDF p. 12, printed p. 70, anchors: exact extraction, stable scaling, and complexity caution).
